items.title: George Guesnon Interview, 1965-09
items.q: Interviewer asks about Ninel Furbus; Interviewee responds with opinions on his style and background ('he's a young son... he's not a jazz musician... he's one of the greatest musicians in New Orleans') but does not describe a direct personal or professional interaction.

ctx.x: And raise advertisements. Yeah, that's what I'm saying. These kind of people, them phonies, you see? But, you know what I mean? As long as they're controlling the money, you can't tell them they're a phony. No. They're going to be in the spotlight of everything with you. You can't tell them nothing because they're controlling the money. See, that's psychology, you see what I mean? If the guy was broke, you could put him out. Yeah. You can't put him out because he becomes the boss. Yeah. Now, whether I'm good or…

Yeah, even in his and our union, man. Shit. Yeah, yeah. Well, I'm telling you, man. I mean, you know. Yeah. This is a mighty four, a mighty four. Oh, now that's a nice little record, too. Ninel Furbus, he's a good man, isn't he? Yeah? Ninel Furbus. Yeah. What's his style? What bunch did he belong to?

Well, I mean, he's a young son, but he started on Emmanuel Perez. He did? Yeah, yeah. He's good, I mean, you know, but he's not a jazz musician. No? He's one of the greatest musicians in New Orleans. He arranges, composes, right now he just says something, write something for twelve pieces. He put it on paper for a twelve piece band, ten piece band. Yeah? Yeah. Writer Ramers. He's a great musician, but he just can't. You know, he ain't no great jazz man, you know? In other words, he's been in the big bands around…
